front: Confidence level in a sensitive info type
back: How much supporting evidence accompanied the pattern. A bare number is low confidence; the same number with keywords and a checksum is high. Keyword: evidence, not certainty.
How many matches must appear before the rule fires. Separates one card in a document from a spreadsheet of ten thousand. Keyword: volume threshold.
Turns a blank form into a pattern so any document derived from that template is recognised. Keyword: the template is the pattern.
Extends detection to text inside images, catching passport scans and screenshots a text scan cannot see. Keyword: images become text.

front: Trainable classifier vs sensitive info type
back: Classifier recognises what a document is about; a SIT recognises a string it contains. Keyword: category vs pattern.
Matches against a hashed upload of the organisation's real data, so almost no false positives. Keyword: in the table or not.
Item labels encrypt and mark content. Container labels govern privacy, external access, and unmanaged device access — they do not encrypt the files inside. Keyword: container does not encrypt.
Further down the list is more restrictive, which is what makes 'justification required to lower a label' meaningful. Keyword: order carries meaning.

front: One sensitivity label at a time
back: An item carries exactly one sensitivity label, unlike retention labels which are a separate independent axis. Keyword: one per item.
Permissions applied by a label persist with the file outside the tenant, which makes labelling a data-centric rather than location-based control. Keyword: leaves with the file.

Client-side runs in the Office app as you type and can merely recommend. Service-side runs in Exchange, SharePoint, and OneDrive on data at rest and cannot recommend. Keyword: only service-side reaches existing files.
Run an auto-labelling policy in simulation first to measure what it would label before switching it on. Keyword: measure before enforce.
Where a user is in scope of several publishing policies, the highest priority applies. Keyword: grant exceptions without rewriting the baseline.
Crawls on-premises file shares and SharePoint Server. Discovery mode first for an inventory, then enforcement to apply labels in place. Keyword: discover then enforce.

front: Encrypt Only vs Do Not Forward
back: Encrypt Only allows any action but forbids removing protection. Do Not Forward additionally blocks forward, print, and copy. Keyword: Do Not Forward is stricter.
Adds branded templates, message expiry, and revocation of an individual message. Works only for messages read through the portal. Keyword: revoke and expire.
Group variations under a parent, and the parent itself cannot be applied. Keyword: parent is a heading.
Shows the current inventory of items carrying a label or sensitive info type. Answers 'where is it now'. Keyword: inventory.
Whether the content is shared outside the organisation. Detection alone is rarely the trigger. Keyword: shared externally.
Blocks the action but lets the user proceed with a business justification, which is recorded. Keyword: friction plus audit trail.

front: DLP test mode with policy tips
back: The standard first deployment step: users are warned, nothing is blocked, and you learn the real false-positive rate. Keyword: warn before block.

front: Rule precedence within a DLP policy
back: Rules run in priority order and the first match applies its actions, with the most restrictive notifications. Keyword: first match wins.
All matching policies contribute and the most restrictive action wins. A block anywhere defeats an allow. Keyword: most restrictive.
Enforcement varies by the user's Insider Risk level — a tip for low risk, a block for elevated. Keyword: risk-based DLP.
Devices must be onboarded using the same onboarding as Defender for Endpoint before endpoint policies do anything. Keyword: onboard first.
Edge is handled natively; other browsers need the extension before uploads can be seen or controlled. Keyword: non-Edge needs it.
Holds access to a file until policy evaluation completes, so unclassified content is not leaked while a scan is pending. Keyword: wait before allowing.
A policy applies in bulk to a location and is invisible. A label applies to an item, is visible, and can trigger disposition review and records. Keyword: bulk vs item.
Targets a query over user, group, or site attributes instead of a static list, so membership stays current. Keyword: query, not list.
Starts the retention clock from an event such as employee departure or contract end rather than from creation. Keyword: clock starts later.
Retention wins over deletion. Content is never deleted while any rule still says keep. Keyword: keep beats delete.
The longest retention period wins when several apply. Keyword: longest keep.
Where SharePoint and OneDrive content under retention goes when a user deletes it — invisible to the user, recoverable by an admin. Keyword: not a backup, but not gone.
Shows every retention setting affecting a given mailbox or site. The tool for 'why is this still here'. Keyword: what applies here.
Independent axes — an item can carry one of each simultaneously. Keyword: not mutually exclusive.
Supplies resignation and performance dates. Without it the departing-employee template has no trigger and silently produces nothing. Keyword: no connector, no trigger.
Policy indicators are switched on in Insider Risk settings before any policy can use them. Keyword: settings first.
A user is only scored after a triggering event such as a resignation date or a high-severity DLP match — not continuously. Keyword: not always watching.
Usernames are anonymised in insider risk alerts by default; separate roles control who can see identities and content. Keyword: privacy by default.
Visual evidence of device activity. Opt-in, explicitly configured, and scoped to specific users and policies. Keyword: never on by default.
The lightweight remediation — a recorded reminder of policy sent to the user, evidencing a proportionate response. Keyword: recorded reminder.
Standard is on by default with 180-day retention. Premium is per-user licensed, gives one year plus a ten-year add-on, and unlocks intelligent events. Keyword: licence per user.
The Audit Premium event showing whether a compromised mailbox was actually read. Not retroactive — the licence must precede the incident. Keyword: was it read.
Content explorer is an inventory of what exists now. Activity explorer is a stream of what has been happening. Keyword: what is vs what happened.
Purview alerts surface alongside other Defender alerts so a DLP match and an endpoint detection can be seen as one incident. Keyword: correlate.
Content search finds and exports but preserves nothing. A case adds holds, custodians, and review sets. Keyword: search does not preserve.
Place the hold before searching — content deleted between search and hold is gone. Keyword: preserve first.
An assistant answers using whatever the user may already open, surfacing over-permissioned content nobody would have found by browsing. Keyword: permissions become discoverable.
Discovers which AI apps are in use, reports prompts and responses involving sensitive data, and offers one-click policies. Keyword: visibility over AI use.
Device onboarding for endpoint signals and the Purview browser extension for third-party AI sites. Keyword: no extension, no third-party visibility.
